text:
No, they don't necessarily contradict each other. They measure different things.

Hansen records the year tree cover (≥30% canopy) was lost. It shows 23 ha of tree cover in 2000 and a 67.7 ha loss event in 2020. JRC GFC2020 is a forest/non-forest map for 2020 that shows 0 ha of forest. By the end of 2020, the trees that Hansen flags as lost were already gone, so JRC showing no forest is consistent with that loss. The 2020 loss is also pre-baseline history and sits outside the 2021–2025 claim.

One oddity is that the 2020 loss (67.7 ha) is larger than the 23 ha of 2000 tree cover. Hansen's loss can include regrowth or planted trees that were cleared after 2000, so I can't explain it from this output alone.

For the post-baseline claim, no loss event of 0.5 ha or more was detected in 2021–2025. Only 0.4 ha of sub-threshold loss appeared in 2021. This doesn't rule out very small or narrow changes, and it isn't a compliance finding.
